Toil UI

Toil UI: a local web app to see and reason about work across Jira, Azure DevOps and GitHub, on toil. Alpha, local only.

Docs / Toil UI

A local web app for seeing work across Jira, Azure DevOps and GitHub, read through toil: one dashboard per dossier, with its stories, pull requests, builds and deployments side by side.

Status: alpha, local only. It runs on your own machine, binds loopback, and reads through toil with your own connections and dossiers, read-only. It is a separate package from toil: installing toil never installs it.

Start it

npx @imagile-dev/toil-ui

It needs Node 24.14 or later and installs one dependency, @imagile-dev/toil, at the exact version it was built with. Until a version shows on npm, run it from a clone of the repository:

npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run build -w ui
node ui/dist/server/toil-ui.js

It prints one URL and keeps running until you press Ctrl+C:

Toil UI 0.1.0-alpha.1 (alpha, local only), on toil 0.1.0-alpha.3
Syncing through toil, read-only, with your own connections and dossiers.
The cache is /home/you/.toil-ui/cache/toil-ui.db, kept 30 days after each sync; toil-ui wipe deletes it.

Open this URL in your browser. It carries this launch's token, so keep it to yourself:
  http://127.0.0.1:53117/?token=<token>

Open that URL. The page trades the token for a session it keeps in memory, and the token leaves the address bar. A reloaded page forgets its session, so open the URL again to get back in. Each start prints a new token. Toil UI opens no browser itself.

toil-ui --sample serves the sample dossiers and the scripted agent the site’s preview uses, with nothing connected to a tracker.

What it reads

Each dashboard reads its dossier the way toil dossiers show describes it: the Jira project, the Azure DevOps project and pipelines, the GitHub repository and project board, and the OpenShift namespace of each environment. Every call runs in-process through @imagile-dev/toil/api, read-only, and toil’s audit log records it with via: "api" and caller: "toil-ui". A call that fails shows on its own panel with toil’s message and fix.

Sync and the cache

The dashboards read from a local cache, which a sync fills. Press Sync now in the Sync panel at the foot of the page. The sync makes the same toil calls the dashboards make, for every dossier, and stores the answers. The work items go through toil’s Open Work Item mapping, with their status changes and the pull requests, builds and deployments that name them.

  • Incremental. After the first sync, Jira and Azure DevOps searches ask only for what changed since the last good sync (updatedSince, five minutes early in case the clocks disagree), and the GitHub board marks the issues whose updatedAt moved. Only those items and their histories are fetched again. Pull requests, builds, deployments and iterations have no “changed since” in toil, so they’re read again each time, bounded as the dashboards bound them.
  • Every page. Each call follows meta.page.nextCursor to the end, up to 200 pages, and fails that source, saying so, rather than keep part of a listing.
  • Each source on its own. Each area a dossier reads (Jira, Bitbucket, Jenkins, OpenShift and so on) is a source with its own state. A source that fails shows toil’s message and fix in the Sync panel, and keeps its last good data, marked stale. The other sources and dossiers aren’t touched. The next sync asks it for everything since its last good sync, so nothing is missed.
  • When. The line under the header says when the data was synced. The panel says when each dossier was synced, and shows a running sync’s progress (requests, pages and retries, from toil’s own progress events).
  • Where. The cache is one SQLite file, cache/toil-ui.db in the data folder, through Node’s built-in node:sqlite, so there’s no native module. It holds ticket content, so it stays on this machine and is readable by your account only.
  • For how long. Anything not synced again within the retention period (30 days by default) is deleted, at start and after each sync.
  • Wiping it. Wipe the cache in the Sync panel deletes it after asking first. toil-ui wipe does the same from a terminal, once toil-ui has stopped: a running Toil UI holds toil-ui.lock in the data folder, and the command refuses while it does. Your trackers are never touched. The next sync fetches everything again.
  • Deleted tickets. An item deleted in its tracker stays in the cache until the retention period ends or you wipe it, since an incremental search only returns items that still exist.

The page can run only the reads the dashboards make: dossiers list and dossiers show, and each area’s search, history, pull request, build and deployment reads. Any other command is refused before it reaches toil, and a change to a tracker is never made from the page.

The lock on the door

Any program on the machine, or a web page using DNS rebinding, can reach a local port, so the server lets in only the browser holding this launch’s token:

  • The token. A random token per start, in the URL it prints. The page trades it for a session id, which it keeps in memory and sends as a header on every API call. Nothing is kept in a cookie: a browser would send one to any other server on 127.0.0.1, whatever its port.
  • The Host header. Only the exact 127.0.0.1:<port> it printed is answered.
  • No CORS. No Access-Control-* header is ever sent. Every POST also needs the page’s own Origin, a JSON body, and the session’s CSRF token.
  • No network but toil’s. It talks to the hosts in your toil connections, and nothing else.

Settings

SettingFlagEnv varDefault
Bind address--hostTOIL_UI_HOST127.0.0.1 (::1 is the other choice)
Port--portTOIL_UI_PORT0: the OS picks a free one
Base path--base-pathTOIL_UI_BASE_PATH/
Data folder--data-dirTOIL_UI_DATA_DIR~/.toil-ui
Retention--retention-daysTOIL_UI_RETENTION_DAYS30 (1 to 3650)

A flag beats its env var. Any bind address other than loopback is refused in this release. The data folder is Toil UI’s own, apart from toil’s ~/.toil/, and holds the cache. A ~ at the start of TOIL_UI_DATA_DIR means your home folder, on Windows too.

Not in this alpha

  • The agent. The agent pane has no adapter yet, and says so when asked.
  • Settings pages for connections and dossiers. Use toil connections and toil dossiers on the CLI.
  • Serving other machines. It is local only.

The package

@imagile-dev/toil-ui ships the server (dist/server/toil-ui.js) and the built app (dist/app/), and nothing else. It has no install scripts and no native addons, spawns no program, and its front end’s framework is built in rather than installed.

Apache-2.0. See NOTICE for what the app bundles.
